# Project plan

## Start-up phase
The project will kick off by establishing the public development repository on GitHub under an open-source GPL-3 license and configuring an isolated, reproducible R environment managed via `renv` lockfiles. The initial setup focuses on reorganizing the baseline codebase (`app.R`, `Discriminante.R`), standardizing CRAN package dependencies, and configuring automated testing frameworks (`testthat` and `shinytest2`). During this phase, the team will curate and validate four benchmark datasets to serve as reproducible test scenarios across all statistical classification procedures and UI interaction flows.

## Technical delivery
Project execution spans six months, organized into two sequential three-month developmental stages:

Stage 1: Stabilization & Architecture (Months 1–3): Focuses on progressive UI enhancement using `bslib`, decoupling monolithic scripts into modular UI and `moduleServer` layers, integrating `datamods` for flexible data importing, consolidating the core package structure (`run_app()`), preparing test benchmark datasets, and designing `testthat` automated test suites.

Stage 2: Validation, Testing & Package Delivery (Months 4–6): Focuses on executing full test suites (`testthat` and `shinytest2`), generating testing reports, resolving identified edge-case defects, verifying Discriminant Analysis calculations against reference datasets, validating environment reproducibility across clean operating systems using `renv`, and publishing comprehensive technical documentation and user guides.

![Activity and Deliverable Timeline](proposal/imagen1.jpg){width=90%}

## Other aspects
Open-Source Licensing & Code Hosting: The consolidated R package will be maintained in a public GitHub repository under the GPL-3 open-source license to encourage community adoption, transparency, and collaborative contributions.

Community Outreach & Dissemination: Project progress and milestones will be communicated to the broader R community through progress posts on the R Consortium Blog, announcement articles upon package stabilization, presentations at R user conferences (such as UseR!), and participation in ISC project update meetings.

## Financial Plan & Budget Breakdown

The total requested funding is $9,994.08 USD, covering 282 hours of direct development labor across two 3-month stages at an hourly rate of $35.44 USD/hour.
